rules.meaning: a slide is drawn smaller or larger than the canvas, so its page shows an empty band or loses an edge
rules.suggestion: make each <section> exactly the canvas size and let its content fill it

rules.meaning: a box carries a thick colored stripe along one side only, the side-tab or top-bar accent
rules.suggestion: remove the stripe; mark the box with a tinted fill, an even hairline border on every side, type weight or an icon

rules.meaning: text is set below presentation size at the 1600px canvas: body text under 28px or a caption or label under 20px
rules.suggestion: raise body text to 28px and captions to 20px or more, and cut words until it fits; a slide holds less text rather than smaller text

rules.meaning: a short word, number or price is split across two lines inside itself
rules.suggestion: widen the column or the cell until the word fits on one line, or set the text smaller within the type scale; a word is never broken

rules.meaning: a chart is drawn so small that its marks vanish and only its labels show
rules.suggestion: give the chart a width and a height of its own, at least 320 by 240 px, instead of letting it shrink inside a flex box

rules.meaning: a part of the slide is drawn partly or wholly outside the slide, so it is cut off at the edge
rules.suggestion: keep every part inside the slide: move or resize it, shorten the text that runs past, or split the slide

rules.meaning: content is drawn outside the box that should hold it, a card, a filled or bordered area or a clipping frame, so it spills out or is cut off
rules.suggestion: give the box room for its content or take the overflowing part out: shorten the text, drop a fixed height, or move the part into a box of its own

rules.meaning: two parts of the slide are drawn over each other: text over text, text over a logo, icon, picture or box
rules.suggestion: move one of them apart from the other, or shorten the text, so no two parts overlap; a part that fills most of the slide is a background and is the one overlap allowed
